package_info.package_manager: N/A (malicious Windows executable dropper distributed via web downloads)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (malware campaign, not a versioned package)
package_info.why_malicious: NullMixer is a dropper that delivers multiple malware families by masquerading as legitimate software installers. It is distributed via malicious websites that use SEO poisoning to lure users searching for cracked software. Upon execution, it drops and executes a variety of malware, including backdoors, stealers, downloaders, and spyware, leading to system compromise and data exfiltration.

execution_context.file_location: Extracted executable from password-protected ZIP archive

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The dropper executable, when run, silently extracts and executes multiple embedded malware binaries (e.g., RedLine Stealer, SmokeLoader, Vidar, etc.) to the system, often to temporary or system directories.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code writes multiple embedded malware payloads to disk and executes them, resulting in the installation of various malware families and subsequent malicious activity.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate installers do not silently drop and execute unrelated malware binaries.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal installers only install the intended software, not multiple unrelated executables.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software bundles may install multiple legitimate components, but with user consent and transparency.
key_indicators: Silent extraction and execution of multiple unrelated binaries
No user notification or consent for additional payloads

execution_context.file_location: Dropped malware binaries (e.g., RedLine Stealer, SmokeLoader, etc.)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Dropped payloads (e.g., RedLine Stealer) enumerate system information, harvest credentials, and exfiltrate data to hardcoded C2 domains/IPs.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After being dropped and executed, the malware payloads collect sensitive data (credentials, files, system info) and send it to attacker-controlled C2 servers.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting and exfiltrating user data to external servers is a hallmark of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not steal credentials or exfiltrate data without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise management tools may collect system info, but with user awareness and to trusted endpoints.
key_indicators: Network connections to known C2 infrastructure
Access to credential stores and sensitive files

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The dropper deletes itself and/or temporary files after execution to hinder forensic analysis.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After dropping and executing payloads, the dropper deletes itself and temporary artifacts to evade detection and hinder analysis.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Self-deletion and anti-forensics are common in malware to avoid detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers do not erase themselves or their logs after installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate updaters may clean up temporary files, but not the installer itself.
key_indicators: Removal of dropped files/logs immediately after execution

attack_chain.action: User visits a malicious website and downloads a password-protected ZIP archive masquerading as legitimate software.
attack_chain.leads_to: User extracts and executes the dropper executable.

attack_chain.action: User executes the dropper, which silently extracts and executes multiple embedded malware payloads.
Dropped malware payloads (stealers, backdoors, etc.) harvest credentials, system info, and exfiltrate data to C2 servers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive data and compromised systems.

attack_chain.action: Dropper deletes itself and temporary files to evade detection and hinder forensic analysis.
attack_chain.leads_to: Reduces evidence of infection, making detection and response more difficult.

behavioral_signatures: Installer or executable that drops and executes multiple unrelated binaries
Silent installation of known malware families
Immediate self-deletion or removal of temporary files after execution
file_indicators: Password-protected ZIP archives containing suspicious executables
Executables with hashes matching known NullMixer, RedLine, SmokeLoader, etc.
Unexpected binaries written to system or temp directories during installation
network_indicators: Connections to known C2 domains/IPs (e.g., azilominehostz.xyz, dll1.stdcdn.com, 185.186.142.166, etc.)
Outbound traffic to suspicious or newly registered domains after installer execution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for the execution of installer files extracted from password-protected archives, especially those downloaded from non-official sources. Flag any installer that writes and executes multiple unrelated binaries. Correlate file hashes with known malware IOCs. Monitor for network connections to known C2 infrastructure immediately following installer execution. Alert on self-deleting executables or installers that remove their own traces post-installation.
